documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
DM/HTN f/u.
S: Doing well. Down to about 85 kg. Some days of the right-side ache, nothing new. No bleeding issues with the IUD. Meds as listed, no missed doses she can think of. Needs fasting labs in spring before her MRI.
O: Vitals as recorded. Lungs clear, heart regular, abdomen soft. No edema.
A/P: T2DM - A1c today. HTN - near goal. Mixed HLD - lipids with spring labs. NASH/adenoma - GI repeating MRI around May/June. Fasting labs ordered for April. Video visit fine for next check if labs look ok.

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit. Patient at home on her lunch break, identity verified with DOB. Consent for telehealth given.

56 yo F with T2DM, HTN, mixed HLD, obesity (BMI now 31), acanthosis nigricans, NASH, hepatic adenoma, endometrial hyperplasia on LNG-IUD. She is planning a move to another state and wants to know how to get a copy of her records for a new doctor there, and how long it takes. No timeline for the move yet.

Home readings today (her cuff and scale): BP 132/86, pulse 78, weight 84.4 kg. No new symptoms.

Reviewed 4/8 labs with her: A1c 7.2, fasting glucose 154, TC 190, LDL 100, HDL 45, TG 250.

Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, levonorgestrel IUD. NKDA.

Plan:
- Records: release form sent through the portal. Full copy to her within about 2 weeks of the signed form; she can also download visit notes and results from the portal now. We can send directly to a new office once she has one.
- Before any move: keep her GI MRI in June and her gyn follow-up; get 90-day refills so there is no gap.
- Diabetes, BP, lipids: continue current meds. A1c every 3-6 months wherever she lands.
- If the move falls through or gets delayed, physical as usual in August.

documents.title: Records copy
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Signed release received 4/29. Complete record copy (notes, labs, imaging, outside letters, immunizations) sent to pt as a secure electronic download link per her request. Pt confirmed receipt by phone.

reports.study: MRI abdomen with and without contrast
reports.text: MRI abdomen without and with IV hepatobiliary contrast. Comparison 05/20/2024. Diffuse hepatic steatosis. The segment 6 lesion measures 2.6 cm, unchanged, with the same arterial enhancement and hepatobiliary-phase hypointensity. No new hepatic lesion. No biliary dilatation. Spleen normal in size. No ascites.
reports.conclusion: Stable 2.6 cm segment 6 hepatocellular adenoma. Hepatic steatosis.

documents.title: Outside MRI received
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Outside MRI abdomen 6/10/2025 received with GI note: "Adenoma stable at 2.6 cm. Next MRI in 2 years." Scanned and routed to PCP.

documents.title: staying!
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Update - the move is off, I'm staying here. So I'm keeping you as my doctor if that's ok! Also got the MRI letter, glad it's the same. Do I still need my physical in August?

documents.title: RE: staying!
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Very glad to keep you. Yes, let's keep the August physical; front desk will confirm the date. The MRI was good news, and GI wants the next one in 2 years.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Preventive visit, 56 yo F.

Interval: move called off, staying local. Liver MRI June stable. Gyn follow-up coming up in the fall. Weight steady 84 kg; still walking most days. No chest pain, dyspnea, abdominal pain beyond the occasional right-side ache, bleeding, urinary or bowel complaints.

Meds: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40, LNG-IUD. NKDA.

Exam: vitals as recorded, BMI 31. Well. Eyes, ears, throat normal. Neck supple. Lungs clear. Heart RRR without murmur. Breasts deferred to mammogram. Abdomen soft, nontender, liver edge just palpable. Skin: acanthosis neck/axillae. Extremities no edema. Feet: no lesions, pulses intact, monofilament normal. Mood bright.

Assessment/Plan:
1. Health maintenance: mammogram due November, order placed. Colonoscopy 2029. Cervical screening: gyn following with the IUD. Vaccines: flu and COVID in October. Eye exam due - reminded.
2. T2DM: A1c and urine albumin today. Metformin.
3. HTN: at goal at home, close in office. Lisinopril 20.
4. Mixed HLD: lipids done April. Atorvastatin 40.
5. NASH, hepatic adenoma: per GI, next MRI 2027.
6. Endometrial hyperplasia: gyn.
RTC 4-6 months.

documents.title: Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: All of your physical labs are stable: A1c holding steady, kidneys and urine protein normal, blood counts normal, liver enzymes in your usual range. Nothing to change.

documents.title: gyn news
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I saw gyn last week. The biopsy they did still shows the thickened lining (hyperplasia), no cancer, but it hasn't gone away with the IUD. She recommends taking out the uterus, tubes and ovaries by laparoscopy. I said yes, it's being scheduled for February when work is slower. They said I need a pre-op visit with you. Is that right?

documents.title: RE: gyn news
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Tammy, thanks for telling me. That makes sense given the hyperplasia hasn't cleared and your other risk factors, and it's good news the biopsy shows no cancer. Yes - book a pre-op visit with me within 30 days of the surgery date (January is perfect). We'll check labs and an ECG and send gyn a clearance letter.

documents.body: Gyn surgical scheduler called: pt's surgery set for 2/18/26, requesting PCP pre-op evaluation with CBC, BMP, ECG within 30 days. Pt has DM f/u 1/7; will add pre-op to a January slot closer to surgery. Fax # for clearance noted in chart.

reports.text: Bilateral digital screening mammography with tomosynthesis. Comparison 11/2023, 03/2022. Scattered fibroglandular density. No suspicious mass, calcifications or architectural distortion. Stable.

documents.title: Pre-operative Evaluation
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
PRE-OP EVALUATION
Procedure: total laparoscopic hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, outside gynecology, planned 2/18/2026.
Indication: endometrial hyperplasia without atypia, persistent on LNG-IUD.

History: 56 yo F. T2DM on metformin, HTN on lisinopril, mixed HLD on atorvastatin, obesity, NASH, hepatic adenoma (stable on MRI 6/2025). Prior laparoscopic cholecystectomy 2014 under general anesthesia without problems. No personal or family anesthesia complications. No bleeding history.
Functional capacity: walks 30+ minutes, climbs two flights of stairs without symptoms (>4 METs). No chest pain, dyspnea, palpitations, syncope, orthopnea or edema.
Meds: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40, LNG-IUD. NKDA.

Exam: vitals as recorded. Airway normal. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft, nontender, healed port scars. No edema.
ECG: normal sinus rhythm, normal.
Labs: CBC, BMP, A1c today.

Assessment: low-risk patient for an intermediate-risk procedure (RCRI 0 - diabetes not on insulin). No further cardiac testing needed.
Recommendations to surgical team:
- Hold metformin morning of surgery; resume once eating.
- Continue atorvastatin.
Clearance letter faxed after labs result.

documents.title: Pre-op clearance
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pre-op labs reviewed by PCP: CBC and BMP normal, A1c stable. Clearance letter, note, ECG and labs faxed to the gynecology surgical office; fax confirmation received. Pt informed through portal.

events.reason: total laparoscopic hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy

conditions.label: Acquired absence of uterus and cervix

medications.reason: removed with the uterus at hysterectomy

reports.text: Specimens: uterus with cervix, bilateral fallopian tubes and ovaries; intrauterine device received separately. Uterus enlarged. Endometrium: hyperplasia without atypia. No carcinoma. Myometrium unremarkable. Cervix: no dysplasia. Bilateral fallopian tubes and ovaries: benign, no significant abnormality.
reports.conclusion: Endometrial hyperplasia without atypia, no carcinoma. Benign cervix, tubes and ovaries.

events.reason: abdominal pain, nausea and vomiting after recent surgery

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: CT abdomen and pelvis with oral contrast. Postoperative changes of recent hysterectomy and salpingo-oophorectomy. Free intraperitoneal air, more than expected for postoperative day 5, with extraluminal oral contrast adjacent to distal small-bowel loops in the pelvis, consistent with small-bowel perforation. Small amount of free fluid in the pelvis. Liver enlarged and low in attenuation, consistent with steatosis. Gallbladder surgically absent. Kidneys normal in size without hydronephrosis. No bowel obstruction.
reports.conclusion: Small-bowel perforation in the pelvis with extraluminal oral contrast and free air.

documents.body:
OUTSIDE HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPT - provider note, faxed 2/24/2026

HPI: POD 5 from total laparoscopic hysterectomy/BSO (2/18, discharged POD 1). Pain began two days ago and has steadily worsened, now diffuse, with nausea and repeated vomiting. Hx DM2, HTN, and longstanding intermittent abdominal discomfort (fatty liver).

Labs: WBC 16.0, Hgb 13.2, Plt 250, Cr 1.0, BUN 18, CRP 25.
CT A/P with oral contrast: small-bowel perforation in pelvis (extraluminal contrast, free air).
MDM: iatrogenic small-bowel perforation after laparoscopic hysterectomy. IV fluids, IV piperacillin-tazobactam, antiemetic, analgesia, NPO. General surgery consulted, to OR.
Dispo: admitted to general surgery.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY - General Surgery (received 3/3/2026 with pathology from 2/18)
Admit 02/23/2026   Discharge 02/28/2026
Patient: Tammy Washington, 56F

Diagnosis: iatrogenic small-bowel perforation following total laparoscopic hysterectomy/BSO (2/18/2026).
Procedure 2/23: diagnostic laparoscopy, laparoscopic primary repair of distal small-bowel injury, washout.
Course: Taken to OR from the ED. Small-bowel injury found in the pelvis and repaired primarily. IV piperacillin-tazobactam. NPO, then diet advanced from POD 2; tolerating regular diet by discharge. Fever and leukocytosis resolved. Metformin held while NPO, resumed with diet. Lisinopril and atorvastatin continued.
Gyn pathology (2/18): endometrial hyperplasia without atypia, no carcinoma; tubes and ovaries benign.
Discharge meds: amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg BID for 7 days; resume home metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40. NKDA.
Follow-up: PCP within 1 week; general surgery clinic 2 weeks; gyn post-op as scheduled.

documents.title: Call from hospital
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called from her hospital room. After the hysterectomy last week she came back to the ED on Monday with fever and belly pain and was found to have a hole in the small intestine; repaired by laparoscopy the same day. Feels much better, eating a little. Expects discharge this weekend. ED note received yesterday, in chart. Will need post-discharge visit within a week - booked 3/5 2:40. Asked her to have the hospital fax the discharge summary.

documents.title: Pharmacy fill history
documents.author: MA
documents.body: External fill history: amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg #14, filled 2/28/2026, prescriber outside general surgery. Metformin, lisinopril, atorvastatin last filled 1/2026 (90-day). Reconciled to med list.

documents.title: Discharge summary and pathology reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Discharge summary (admit 2/23-2/28) and 2/18 surgical pathology reviewed. Small-bowel perforation after TLH/BSO, laparoscopic repair, pip-tazo then amox-clav x7 days. Pathology: hyperplasia without atypia, no carcinoma, adnexa benign. Problem list and meds updated (IUD off, s/p hysterectomy). TCM visit 3/5 confirmed.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-discharge visit (TCM). Contact made by RN 2/25 while inpatient; discharge summary received 3/3 and reviewed.

Course: TLH/BSO 2/18 for endometrial hyperplasia without atypia, home POD 1. Returned 2/23 with fever, tachycardia, peritonitic abdomen; CT showed small-bowel perforation; laparoscopic repair same day; IV pip-tazo; home 2/28 on amox-clav. Pathology benign, hyperplasia without atypia, no cancer.

Today: no fever since discharge. Eating normally, bowels moving. Mild soreness at port sites. Two doses of antibiotic left. Back on metformin, lisinopril, atorvastatin. Blood sugars 130s-160s.

Exam: vitals as recorded, afebrile. Appears well. Abdomen soft, appropriately mildly tender around incisions, no distension, port sites clean and dry without redness. Bowel sounds normal.

A/P:
1. Iatrogenic small-bowel perforation s/p laparoscopic repair - recovering well. Finish amox-clav. CBC and BMP today. Surgical clinic follow-up next week. Return precautions: fever, worsening pain, vomiting, redness or drainage at incisions.
2. S/p TLH/BSO - endometrial hyperplasia treated; removed from active problems. IUD removed with uterus, off med list. Post-op gyn visit as scheduled.
3. T2DM - continue metformin.
4. HTN, mixed HLD - continue.
Med reconciliation completed. RTC May.

documents.title: Labs from yesterday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your white count is back to normal and your kidney tests and electrolytes are fine. Rest up and keep walking short distances. See you in May.

documents.title: checkups done
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Just an update: saw the surgeon and the gyn this month for my post-op checks. Both said everything is healing fine. Going back to work part time next week, full time in April.

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u DM, HTN, and after February surgery/complication.

S: Back at work full time since April. No abdominal pain, normal appetite and bowel habits. Incisions healed. Surgeon and gyn released her. Walking again. Admits the winter set her back on exercise. Taking all meds.

O: Vitals as recorded. Abdomen soft, nontender, well-healed port sites. No hernia felt. Feet normal.

A/P:
- Iatrogenic bowel perforation, repaired - fully recovered. Resolved.
- T2DM: A1c and urine albumin today; metformin 1000 BID.
- HTN: lisinopril 20.
- Mixed HLD: atorvastatin 40, lipids at physical.
- NASH/hepatic adenoma: liver panel today; GI MRI due 2027.
PHQ-9 3 - reasonable after a hard winter, no concerns voiced.
Physical in August.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual preventive visit. 57 yo F.

Since May: feeling well, no abdominal symptoms, back to walking most evenings. No hot flashes to speak of since surgery. No new concerns.

Problems: T2DM, HTN, mixed hyperlipidemia, obesity, metabolic syndrome, acanthosis nigricans, NASH, hepatic adenoma (stable 6/2025), s/p TLH/BSO 2/2026 (benign), s/p repaired small-bowel perforation 2/2026, s/p cholecystectomy 2014.
Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily. NKDA.

Exam: vitals as recorded. Well. HEENT normal. Neck no thyromegaly or nodes. Lungs clear. Heart RRR. Abdomen soft, nontender, liver edge just palpable, healed port sites. Skin: acanthosis neck/axillae. Ext no edema. Feet: intact, pulses normal, monofilament normal. Neuro nonfocal. Mood good.

Health maintenance:
- Mammogram 11/2025 negative; next 11/2026-2027.
- Colonoscopy 2019 normal; next 2029.
- Cervical screening no longer needed (hysterectomy for benign disease, prior screening normal).
- Vaccines: Shingrix, PCV20, Hep B, Tdap 2018 complete. Flu/COVID this fall. Tdap due 2028.
- Eye exam due September.
- PHQ-2 0.

Plan: fasting labs drawn (CMP, lipids, CBC, A1c). Continue current medications. Diabetes follow-up in November.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Tammy, labs from the physical: A1c steady, LDL about the same as last year, triglycerides still high, kidneys and blood counts normal, liver enzymes in your usual range. No medication changes. See you in November.
